data.narrative:
Grain Weevil is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chad and Ben Johnson that has raised $3.5M to date. The comparable universe includes one public peer (277810.KQ) and eight private robotics firms, among them Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI, though a sufficiently narrow peer set meeting stage and valuation criteria does not exist for reliable median-based triangulation.

The stage-progression method is applicable here, using the $3.5M raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage step-ups in robotics, yielding an implied valuation of $9M. This represents the primary quantitative anchor given the constraint that peer-median analysis requires three or more comparable datapoints at similar stage and tier; while eleven same-sector peers exist, filtering for seed or adjacent-stage companies with comparable valuation tiers leaves insufficient depth for robust comparison.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $7M to $10M, centered at $9M. Key uncertainties include the absence of a deep comparable cohort at identical stage and scale, which limits confidence in stage-progression assumptions. Refinement would require either access to a broader private market dataset for robotics seed fundings or follow-on fundraising activity from Grain Weevil itself to validate assumptions about investor step-up behavior in this subsector.
